source.title: Exploring Robust Overfitting for Pre-trained Language Models

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether adversarial training on pretrained language models develops a gap between training and test robustness, and reports that gap along with conditions that mitigate it. This is adversarial robustness, not the natural-label generalization in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The results concern adversarial examples and robust training/test loss or accuracy. They do not test the claim versions' natural-label generalization. Figure-only sweeps are not assigned reconstructed numeric values.
record.test_reason: The study measures adversarial generalization and robust overfitting in pretrained language models. None of V1–V8 concerns this construct. Its dropout sweep measures robust performance in transformers, not the natural-label classifier performance specified in V6. Citations to standard generalization findings provide background rather than tests.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors identify robust overfitting in pretrained language models, attribute it to memorization of adversarial training data, and report that suitable flooding levels mitigate it under PGD evaluation. Dropout and weight decay contribute little; TextFooler benefits vary by training method. The memorization explanation is their interpretation, rather than a direct influence-based measurement.
record.recipe_differences: Studies adversarial training and robust loss/accuracy on pretrained NLP models, rather than standard natural-label training and natural-label generalization.
record.method_sensitivity: Adversarial training method, dataset, model architecture, PGD attack iterations, dropout ratio, weight-decay coefficient, flooding level, and attack type affect measured robust loss or accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Robust test loss increases while adversarial training loss rapidly approaches zero; re-attacks and stronger evaluation attacks reveal limited adversarial generalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretrained language models can exhibit robust overfitting during adversarial training.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing dropout or weight decay does not reliably mitigate robust overfitting; large settings harm robust accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Conventional regularization can fail to improve adversarial generalization in pretrained language models.

fits_no_version.finding: Suitable flooding levels reduce PGD robust overfitting and prevent perfect adversarial training accuracy, while flooding alone provides little TextFooler robustness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Flooding can improve PGD adversarial generalization when combined with adversarial training, with benefits depending on its level.

fits_no_version.finding: Flooding increases TextFooler robust accuracy with FreeLB and InfoBERT but decreases it with TAVAT on both reported dataset/model combinations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benefits from flooding depend on the adversarial training method and evaluation attack.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Findings of ACL 2023)
record.problems: The paper reports single-run results and no error bars. Many sweeps are shown only in figures, with qualitative descriptions rather than exact values. It focuses on PGD-based robust overfitting; the authors note textual-attack findings may differ.
record.rows_left_out: No results left out. Figure 10 and Figure 11 contain additional qualitative plot results across datasets, architectures, and adversarial search steps; the prose does not assign separate precise outcomes to every plotted curve, so no numeric rows were reconstructed.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label held-out generalization.
Width-dependent test error beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classification and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove the penalty.
Dropout's effect on natural-label held-out error in fully connected and convolutional classifiers, including dataset-size and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps relative to other measures.
Removing examples selected by label-memorization influence versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All rows remain linked to none. Their states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8, even where the paper clearly establishes its separate robustness findings. No version-relevant missing results were identified.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test accuracy.
Width sweeps and natural-label test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image models.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers and natural-label held-out performance.
Dropout's effect on natural-label held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the natural-label generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring natural-label test accuracy.

rows.operation_detail: FreeLB adversarial training with dropout ratios varied in attention probabilities and fully connected layers
rows.measure: Robust test loss and robust accuracy across epochs
rows.value: Robust loss decreases as dropout ratio increases, but still increases with epoch; robust accuracy also decreases as dropout ratio increases.

rows.subject: BERT-base
rows.operation_detail: FreeLB adversarial training with dropout ratios varied in attention probabilities and fully connected layers
rows.measure: Robust test loss and robust accuracy across epochs
rows.value: At dropout ratios in [0.7, 0.9], robust test loss begins to decrease rather than increase, but robust test accuracy remains low; large dropout hurts robust test performance.
rows.note: Lower loss accompanies low accuracy, so authors say large dropout only ostensibly alleviates robust overfitting.
rows.check: High dropout harms robust performance, but this is not a test of V6 in its specified systems and outcome.

rows.subject: BERT-base
rows.operation_detail: FreeLB adversarial training with weight-decay coefficient varied
rows.measure: Robust test loss and robust test accuracy across epochs
rows.value: Weight decay cannot avoid robust overfitting; coefficients 5 and 10 make robust test loss smaller in later epochs, but too-large λ increases robust test loss overall; large coefficients hurt robust accuracy, small coefficients have little effect.
rows.note: The text reports qualitative comparisons across coefficients, not exact plotted values.
rows.check: A weight-decay sweep on robust performance does not test any listed version.

relation.reason: The introduction discusses standard generalization and memorization, but the study's own experiments neither test a listed version nor use its specific finding as a tool.

tranche.reason: The study measures adversarial overfitting and its mitigation in pretrained transformers, a different construct from V1–V8. Its dropout sweep evaluates adversarial robustness rather than V6's specified classifier generalization.

source_check.notes: The memorization explanation is the authors' interpretation; these experiments do not test V1–V8. Table 1's caption inconsistently mentions FreeLB despite describing training without AT, and does not explicitly identify its dataset.
